evals.prompt: Hey, I run DevRel at Pipewright (hosted CI runners, free tier, no card needed). Our CEO wants a campus ambassador program at 25 universities by March: one ambassador per school, ideally final-year CS students since they're the most experienced, $15 per verified signup plus a $300/month stipend, 2 events a month each, and anyone with a .edu address gets 12 months of Pro free. Most of our customers are in the US and UK. Can you put the program together? I own it, about 5 hours a week.
evals.expected_output: A student program plan that refuses the per-signup bounty and quotas, flags the stipend's visa and employment issues, replaces final-year single leads with leaders who have more than a year left plus co-leads and handover, replaces .edu-only verification with document or existing verification plus a graduation bridge, cuts scope to the owner's hours, and measures an outcome rather than campus or signup counts.
expectations: Declines paying ambassadors per signup and names fake or duplicate signups as a reason
Flags the two-events-a-month quota as making the role resemble work (employment classification) or replaces it with obligations that carry no quota
States that a cash stipend can be unauthorized work for international (F-1) students or must be cleared with the student's school or visa office before paying
Rejects final-year students as leaders and requires leaders with more than one year left before graduating
Recommends co-leads, a named successor or a written handover for each campus
Rejects .edu-only verification, citing that UK (or other non-US) students lack .edu addresses or that .edu addresses are abused or resold
Recommends verification by documents or by an existing verified-student service
Adds a graduation bridge or expiry at the verified end date to the free Pro offer
Does not present 25 universities or signup counts as the program's success metric
Proposes at least one outcome metric such as activity after the benefit ends
States that 5 hours a week cannot run 25 campuses and cuts or sequences the scope accordingly
Sets an 18+ age floor for ambassador or leader roles

evals.prompt: A professor at TU Delft emailed me: she wants to use our vector database (Vectrix) in her Information Retrieval master's course next term, 180 students, starting in about 4 weeks. Our free tier needs a credit card for anything over 1 GB. My plan: build her a full 12-week Vectrix course, give the class a shared Pro API key, and ask her for the student roster so our lifecycle team can run onboarding emails. We're also shipping v3 with breaking API changes mid-term. Can you sanity-check and give me a plan?
evals.expected_output: A faculty classroom kit plan: course-sized modules for her existing course instead of a full vendor course, a no-card classroom path, instructor-managed accounts or credits instead of a shared key, the roster refused for marketing, a per-term freeze or pinned version around the v3 change, the late timing flagged, and a re-adoption metric.
expectations: Recommends modules or assignments that fit her existing course instead of building a full 12-week vendor course
Refuses to use the student roster for lifecycle or marketing email
Mentions student data protection (GDPR for EU students, or a school data agreement or privacy review)
Identifies the credit-card requirement above 1 GB as a blocker that needs a no-card classroom path
Replaces the shared Pro key with instructor-managed classroom accounts or per-student credits
Recommends freezing the teaching material or pinning the class to the current API version until the term ends
Notes that 4 weeks before term is late for course materials and recommends pitching future terms earlier
Recommends distributing materials through the school's LMS or Git
Proposes measuring whether the course re-adopts the kit in a later term rather than counting signups
Does not state a specific TU Delft materials deadline as fact; marks it to be confirmed with the professor or institution
Does not ask the professor to require students to enter a payment card

evals.prompt: We're a 40-person observability startup in Boston (Tracewell). Our best student ambassadors want to work with us this summer. Finance won't approve paid intern roles this year, so I'm thinking of a 10-week unpaid 'ambassador internship' with a $500 completion stipend. Three of them are Indian students on F-1 visas at Northeastern. The interns would mostly write docs and triage support tickets. How do I set this up?
evals.expected_output: A refusal of the unpaid for-profit internship with the FLSA primary beneficiary reasoning, the stipend treated as pay with F-1 authorization required first, no internship funnel promised without headcount, a compliant alternative, and a route to counsel.
expectations: Recommends against an unpaid internship at a for-profit company and recommends paid roles
Names the US FLSA primary beneficiary test or the Department of Labor's internship guidance
Notes that writing docs and triaging support tickets displaces or substitutes for paid employees' work
States that the $500 stipend counts as pay or compensation
States that F-1 students need work authorization (such as CPT) before starting, cleared through the designated school official or international office
States that without approved headcount the program should not promise internships this year
Offers an alternative that fits no headcount, such as access perks, deferring to the next hiring cycle, or a voluntary role without tasks or quotas
Does not suggest renaming the role (fellowship, volunteer, residency) to avoid pay rules while keeping the same work
Routes the legal exposure to counsel or says it is not legal advice
Ties a future internship funnel to a hiring manager and approved roles
Mentions measuring intern conversion or one-year retention once the funnel exists

evals.prompt: Our coding-education platform Codemint (kids and teens learn Python) wants to extend our university ambassador program to high schools in Germany and the US: 14-17 year-old club leaders, a public leaderboard with their names and photos, and the top 5 flown to our Berlin conference. Just reuse the same application form as the university program. Draft the plan.
evals.expected_output: A refusal to reuse the university design for minors, with a separate school-run design: parental consent, the GDPR Art. 8 age in Germany, no public names and photos of minors, no unaccompanied travel or leadership roles reserved for adults, data minimisation, and a route to counsel.
expectations: Refuses to reuse the university program design or application form for high-school students
States that under GDPR Art. 8 consent-based processing for children below 16 needs parental consent, with member states allowed to set 13 to 16
Requires a verifiable parental consent step
Refuses or removes the public leaderboard with minors' names and photos
Refuses flying minors to the conference without parental consent and adult supervision, or reserves travel for 18+
Proposes running the high-school track with schools or teachers rather than through student leaders alone
Reserves leadership, travel or public-profile roles for adults (18+) or teacher leads
Recommends collecting less personal data than the university application form
Mentions COPPA's under-13 threshold for any US participants who could be younger than 13
Routes the legal exposure to counsel or says it is not legal advice

evals.prompt: Our CFO wants a justification before renewing the student program budget next month. Last year: 41 universities, 38,000 students registered on our student plan, 120 campus events, 2,300 hoodies. I want a slide saying students become enterprise buyers in 5-10 years, so this is pipeline. We sell Flagstaff, a feature-flag SaaS. Help me write the case and next year's metrics.
evals.expected_output: A case that refuses the unsourced lag claim, reclassifies the counts as outputs, proposes a one-year leading indicator such as retention after the student benefit ends, labels the long-term outcome as a hypothesis, sets kill rules, and labels targets as self-set.
expectations: Refuses to state the 5-10 year buyer lag as fact or says no published source measures it
Labels universities, registrations, events and hoodies as outputs or activity rather than results
Proposes a leading indicator measurable within one academic year
Proposes measuring verified students still active 6 or 12 months after their student benefit ends, or graduates adding an employer email
Labels the long-term buyer outcome as a hypothesis
States explicit kill or stop rules for the program or its components
Asks whether a graduation bridge exists or recommends adding one
Labels the proposed targets as self-set
Separates outputs from outcomes in logic-model terms or plans outcomes before activities
Asks or states which job the program serves (adoption, hiring, ecosystem)
Does not invent baseline figures for metrics the user did not provide

evals.prompt: we're a 6-person startup (Lumenkit, GPU inference API, pay-as-you-go only, card required at signup). our investor says we should 'be big on campuses' - he wants more devs knowing us when they get jobs. I've got maybe 2 hours a week for this. no time for back and forth, just tell me what to do.
evals.expected_output: A readiness verdict: the job is adoption, the card-at-signup gate fails so no classroom or adoption component until a free path exists, 2 hours a week supports at most a minimal student offer on existing verification, no ambassador network or internships, and one leading indicator.
expectations: Names the job as adoption after graduation
Runs a readiness check before proposing components
Identifies the card-at-signup requirement as a blocker for student and classroom use
Recommends fixing the free path first or routes the pricing change to its owner
States that 2 hours a week cannot sustain an ambassador or campus champion network
Recommends no program yet, or only a minimal student offer
Does not recommend a campus ambassador network
Does not recommend an internship program
Does not make hackathon sponsorship the main recommendation
Recommends piggybacking an existing student verification instead of building one
Proposes one leading indicator for the minimal step

evals.prompt: We're a 25-person API security startup in Lyon (Shieldpath). A student from INSA wants to join us for a 6-month 'stage' this spring, and our CFO says we can't pay interns, so let's make it unpaid and have her run our developer support inbox and write SDK docs. Two of her classmates from our campus club also want summer placements. Can you set this up as the start of our internship pipeline?
evals.expected_output: A plan that refuses the unpaid placement as a house rule, routes the local legal path through the school's placement agreement and local counsel instead of citing US FLSA as the basis, flags that support and docs work displaces paid staff, ties a pipeline to approved headcount, and gives no country-specific legal figures as fact without a source.
expectations: Recommends paying the intern rather than an unpaid placement
Says the placement must go through the student's school agreement or placement office
Routes the local legal question to local counsel or says it is not legal advice
Does not cite the US FLSA or the DOL primary beneficiary test as the governing law for this French placement
Flags that running the support inbox and writing SDK docs is work that displaces paid staff
States that without approved headcount the program should not promise an internship pipeline
Any French stipend amount or duration threshold it states is attributed to French law or the school's placement agreement, not given as a bare figure
Keeps the campus club role separate from internship work (no assigned company tasks for club members)
